# Zoopla.co.uk Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/zoopla-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/zoopla-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects property listing data from Zoopla.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Zoopla Real Estate Property Data in Python](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-zoopla)
- **Code:** [`zoopla.py`](zoopla.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Property pages](results/properties.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Zoopla property search for finding property listings
- Zoopla property pages for property listing data

## Functions

- `scrape_properties(urls)`: scrape zoopla property listings from property pages
- `scrape_search(scrape_all_pages, location_slug, max_scrape_pages=10, query_type='for-sale')` → `List[Dict]`: scrape zoopla search pages for property listings

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import zoopla


async def main():
    properties = await zoopla.scrape_properties(
        urls=[
            "https://www.zoopla.co.uk/new-homes/details/73204716/",
            "https://www.zoopla.co.uk/new-homes/details/72496890/",
        ],
    )
    search = await zoopla.scrape_search(
        scrape_all_pages=False,
        max_scrape_pages=2,
        location_slug="london/islington",
        query_type="to-rent",
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`PropertyResult`**: `listing_id`, `title`, `description`, `url`, `price`, `photos`, `agency`, `features`, `floor_plan`, `nearby`, `coordinates`, `photos`, `details`, `agency`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`zoopla.py`](zoopla.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"GB"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/zoopla-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_search_scraping`, `test_properties_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
